plan.summary: A standard 12-month run on AstraZeneca PLC (AZN ADR, NYSE), base currency USD, as of 2026-09-25, answering three operator questions: revenue exposure to exclusivity events dated inside the horizon, whether the oncology pipeline is already in the price, and what US pricing policy does to the margin path. The priced-in question is bounded by published consensus (third-party opinion, not fact) alongside an implied-expectations solve. The revenue-to-margin bridge for pricing haircuts is an explicit labelled assumption and a sensitivity axis, not a figure derived from filings. This plan states no figures; prior research is background only and never cited.

challenges.statement: The second operator question is about what the market expects, yet no planned source establishes market expectations. The source list has price and share count only. challenges.suggestion: Add an expectations source: published consensus revenue/EPS estimates and their dispersion, plus ADR price reaction over dated windows around prior oncology readouts and approvals. Label consensus as third-party opinion, not fact, and use it to bound the implied solve.

challenges.statement: industry_landscape covers pricing mechanics and generic/biosimilar entry, but no section asks what competing branded assets do to the in-line oncology franchise or to the value of the Phase III pipeline. Revenue inside a 12-month horizon can fall from a rival's approval or superior readout with no patent event at all, and pipeline assets compete for the same indications. The plan's erosion model is exclusivity-only.
challenges.suggestion: Extend industry_landscape and catalysts to name competitor assets filed or reading out in the same indications, sourced from FDA approval records and clinicaltrials.gov registry entries, and treat competitive displacement as a separate erosion channel from exclusivity loss.

challenges.statement: valuation_dcf takes its margin path from industry_landscape, and scenarios_sensitivities runs 'negotiated-price haircuts for any selected medicines'. No planned source can establish that bridge, so the margin effect of pricing policy rests on an unstated assumption.
